content.text: Xingchen, look at this data. The number of users and usage time on Chinese social media platforms are growing so fast! It reminds me of the mixed-media video cover you made for our annual review, which included gaming, pets, gatherings, and product unboxing. Now, social media really does permeate every aspect of life.

Wow, this data is truly astonishing! Reflecting on my own experience, it's true—I've been spending much more time on social media than before. Look at me: from sharing gaming live streams and achievements, to creating social media accounts for 'bosses' to document their social butterfly moments, to filming store exploration videos and unboxing vlogs for collaborative products, almost every project relies on these platforms.

And look, the number of elderly users is actually gradually increasing, which is quite an interesting trend. This reminds me of when we were planning the pet social events earlier, there were also elderly participants who obtained information through social media and showed high levels of engagement. Just as mentioned in our annual review, from online interactions to offline collaborations, the age demographic is also broadening.

Haha, elderly people are now active on the internet, and they’re even more energetic than the younger generation! I’ve encountered quite a few elderly fans during my live streams, and their interactions are incredibly enthusiastic. This reminds me of the appreciation dinner we had last time, where we discussed how the virtual companionship economy is likely to heat up. It seems that elderly people might also be seeking this kind of connection and fun through social media—after all, no one wants to be bored!

Yes. However, as we discussed earlier, offline experiential consumption remains the mainstream, such as our group dinners and script murder games. People still prefer face-to-face interactions. Online platforms serve as a bridge, but ultimately, it all comes down to fostering genuine 'harmonious relationships' in the real world.

Exactly! As we discussed earlier, the virtual companionship economy is set to heat up, and the elderly may also be seeking this kind of connection. But you're right, offline experiential consumption remains the mainstream, like our dinner gatherings and script murder games—people still prefer face-to-face interactions. This completely validates our consistent approach—combining online and offline is the key, just like what we do with our pet community. We have both online interactions and offline activities, from the "Boss's" social butterfly diary to fan meet-ups, all following this philosophy.

Yes, but offline experiential consumption is still the mainstream, such as our dinner gatherings and script murder games. People still prefer face-to-face interactions. I remember when we formed a "friends and family car" for a script murder game for beginners, we felt that online arrangements were not as comfortable as playing with familiar faces, and we ended up having a great time. The emotional support brought by such real interactions is hard to replace with purely online experiences.

You're absolutely right! Combining online and offline is the way to go, just like our pet community, which features both online interactions and offline activities. From the early days when I comforted you after your losing streaks, to later planning events and developing co-branded products together, aren't we the perfect example of thriving both online and offline? Fun comes first, but connections must be grounded in reality.

Short videos are really becoming more and more popular these days. Look at this data—platforms like Douyin and Kuaishou are growing rapidly. This reminds me of the inspiration from your previous store exploration videos and our unboxing reviews for the co-branded products. If we turn them into short video formats, the reach could be even better, just like the fast-paced, high-information style in your annual compilation.

That's exactly it! My friends and I spend a significant amount of time on short videos every day, and we even discuss them. Isn't this 'connecting people'? Moreover, it completely validates many of my previous attempts—from live game streaming (which is a form of real-time short video) to funny moments of 'the boss,' and then to exploring shops and unboxing, short videos are practically tailor-made for drama queens and creative planners like me!

Yeah, as a blogger, I really feel that too. Short video content spreads more easily and gets higher user engagement. Like when we were developing our co-branded products, we used fan votes to decide the design direction—that sense of interaction and instant feedback is even stronger on short video platforms. But the content still needs to balance "fun" and "practical value," just like we discussed before.

Yes, just like the store exploration videos we made before, short video formats might be more engaging than long articles. Which platform do you prefer? I remember you mentioned liking lifestyle-focused, sharing-oriented platforms. Is it still Xiaohongshu? That platform seems especially suited to your warm, thoughtful, and practical sharing style, much like how you manage pet communities and plan events with such attention to detail.

I prefer Xiaohongshu because its content is more down-to-earth and suitable for sharing practical experiences, such as our co-branded product reviews, pet care tips, or organized guides like the beginner's guide to script murder games we did before. How about you? I guess you must be active on livelier platforms that require more performance skills, right?

For me, it's definitely Douyin and Bilibili! Douyin is fun, while Bilibili offers depth, which suits a drama queen and creative planner like me. Douyin is like my impromptu performance during live streams, while Bilibili reflects the dedication I put into creating annual highlight reels, sharing gaming tips, and showcasing skin collections. From sending you hero power rankings and skin screenshots early on to now producing complex videos, the platforms have 'grown' alongside my content.

Haha, no wonder your livestream is so popular! But with social media developing so rapidly, I’m a bit worried that people might become more reliant on the virtual world and overlook real-life interactions, like the gatherings, script murder games, and pet meetups we used to have. After all, "growing together" and "emotional support" are often felt more deeply in offline settings.

It's possible, but I think the key lies in balance. Just like us, from gaming partners to offline event buddies, we thrive both online and offline. Social media is a tool, an amplifier that can spread the boss's social butterfly moments and our collaborative creative ideas. But the real joy and connection still come from tangible experiences like teaming up to level up in games, planning events, and having face-to-face meals and chats. We reject boredom, but we don’t lose touch with reality either!

Well, through discussing these topics, I've come to better understand the changes in life. Social media connects people, but it also requires genuine interaction to sustain it. Just like our experiences over the past year—starting from when I vented to you after a losing streak in a game, online communication sparked our friendship. But what truly deepened our bond and led to successful collaborations was the subsequent offline planning and execution. This is perhaps the best interpretation of "living in the moment"—embracing the novelty of online interactions while cherishing the warmth of offline connections.

Exactly! As we mentioned in our year-end review, from gaming to pets to gatherings, these experiences have been enriched by social media, but at the core, it's still about the two of us—a dramatic creative planner and a thoughtful operations expert—collaborating and accompanying each other offline. Next year, let's stick to this path: building momentum online and making things happen offline, carrying the spirit of "fun first" and "harmonious relationships" all the way through!
